message.subject: Re: Stage38 explicit RELEASE
message.body:
Stage38 gate-by-gate verification complete. Every number in timing-comparison.json reproduces exactly, all six performance gates PASS, and the correctness, host and provenance prerequisites are clean. engineering_accepted=true is supported on the evidence in the tree. Source-only, read-only, no reruns, nothing under /tmp/enola-hash-read-diagnostic/ or your worktree modified.

GOVERNING TEXT AND HARNESS INTEGRITY. I verified against bounded-hash/PROMOTION_RULE.md, 13 lines, sha256 6724a0d8f8c6015c40e1c21415e1e1a77fb0fb02bf55f5e5f70af3857371476d, the copy pinned in cli-pairs/pins.json. I hash-pinned all twenty harness scripts BEFORE opening any result file, so the thresholds I checked against cannot have been read back from the outcome. final/summarize-timing.py is byte-identical to the Stage37 accepted copy except one hunk: the primary gain threshold changes from at most -2 to at most -3 percent, which is exactly the frozen 0.97 ratio. No other logic differs. The validator pin at line 62 raises before exec_module, and the binary pin check at lines 81-84 runs before any arithmetic, so both are fail-closed.

SOURCE IDENTITY. The three changed files at 1af548c hash exactly to source-equivalence.json: buffered_hash.go dab645c5, buffered_hash_test.go 27c39eb4, engine.go 16e96043. The candidate binary is e9e48eb0eaeb4e642ff6078ee4a5db0b65eda9d545b61e935ee9f330bb6e1805; note for the archive that this is a binary digest, not a revision, and does not resolve as one. git diff --name-only 1af548c c4f0a2b over internal, cmd, pkg and go files is EMPTY, so cb6a69f and c4f0a2b add only docs and archive material and the source I reviewed in msg_f04619eb67a2 is precisely the source that was timed.

SIX PERFORMANCE GATES, with margins so the narrowness is on record.

1. Primary fresh-process no-op ratio of medians at most 0.97: PASS at 0.931736155, -6.826384 percent. Baseline median 2.006361625 s; the candidate was allowed at most 1.946170776 s and delivered 1.869399666 s, so 76.77 ms of headroom, 3.826 pp. This is the widest primary margin of any cohort I have verified.

2. All six paired no-op ratios below 1: PASS, and not marginally. Per pair: 0.926122 (-7.3878, -151.07 ms), 0.930826 (-6.9174, -139.49 ms), 0.928478 (-7.1522, -143.79 ms), 0.938157 (-6.1843, -123.41 ms), 0.930002 (-6.9998, -139.95 ms), 0.931810 (-6.8190, -136.54 ms). The worst pair still keeps 6.18 percent and 123 ms. Leave-one-pair-out on the primary, as a robustness note and not a subset analysis, gives 0.932255, 0.932255, 0.935007, 0.928478, 0.931219, 0.931219 - every one clears 0.97, so the primary verdict does not depend on any single pair.

3. Non-primary median regressions at most 2 percent: PASS, and all three are improvements rather than regressions: initial -1.155406, body -3.822325, structural -3.380370 percent. No scenario needs the bound.

4. Every scenario median RSS increase at most 5 percent: PASS at initial -1.570533 (-19.594 MiB), no-op +1.099927 (+3.867 MiB), body +4.293269 (+35.898 MiB), structural -2.520046 (-22.000 MiB).

5. Mean of the four scenario median-time ratios below 1: PASS at 0.9620387859422697.

6. Sum of scenario median seconds nonincreasing: PASS at 21.211849625572 to 20.658953749517 s, -552.90 ms, -2.606542502492 percent. Every term is negative: initial -129.82, no-op -136.96, body -144.54, structural -141.58 ms. No scenario is paying for another, which is the first cohort in this series where that is true.

COUNTERBALANCING AND WINDOW. Realized order is B1 C1, C2 B2, B3 C3, C4 B4, B5 C5, C6 B6 - AB BA AB BA AB BA, three of each, as required. No subsetting, pooling or re-selection anywhere: all twelve arms are present, all exit 0, none errored, and there is no thirteenth arm directory, so no refill. All twelve ran 18:26:50 to 18:42:15 UTC, entirely inside the granted window and entirely after the not_before_utc 18:25:25 you recorded, using 15.4 of the 45 minutes. I confirmed the ordering is strictly sequential and non-overlapping.

HOST CONDITIONS. Pressure: 3519 samples across twelve files, every one Darwin dispatch level 1, worst gap 0.2755 s against the one-second rejection threshold, zero sampler errors, and every arm bracketed at both ends (first sample 0.1-0.3 ms before monotonic_start, last about 0.1 ms after monotonic_end). Suspension: per-arm series drift is +2127 to +2251 ms, which is the known instrumentation constant for run-timing-series.py and matches prior accepted cohorts by the same formula; the actual fine-grained detector, the per-sample wall-minus-monotonic offset, spreads only 0.242 to 1.185 ms with mean 0.339 ms, so there was no sleep anywhere. Swap: zero new Swapouts in all twelve arms; Swapins 20 to 224 per arm, reported as context only with no disqualifying effect. Power: 24 of 24 boundary observations on AC with lowpowermode 0; charge declines monotonically 41 to 33 percent, minimum 33 well above the 20 percent floor.

CORRECTNESS, recomputed rather than read off your flags. 84 of 84 label runs exit 0. Exactly one distinct graph hash per label across all twelve arms: 194f7fbfbfa36deb for initial, no-op, body, cold-body and cold-original, and 777ca16850b64c1b for structural and cold-structural. Both values are identical to Stage37's, so this is cross-binary AND cross-stage graph equality. Incremental equals cold in 36 of 36 comparisons. All twelve no-ops are silent: state_before equals state_after, zero wire messages, parsed_files 0, files_read 0, cached_files 6801, and no wire object at all. Broker: 72 of 72 published-label observations report completeness_status success with batch_count_matches_end never false. The twelve per-arm no-op state digests are distinct, which is expected; cross-arm byte identity is not a claim and never was.

PUBLICATION CONTENT. Wire tuples are exactly two per label, one per arm, differing ONLY in payload_bytes_total: +3084 on initial and all three cold labels (104851501 to 104854585, 104883405 to 104886489, 104863837 to 104866921, 104876173 to 104879257), +3 on body (1010 to 1013), +4 on structural (20957 to 20961). This is the run-identifier-length arithmetic already accepted in Stage37 - 3081 batches at one byte each plus two for begin and one for end - and it is a harness naming artifact, not candidate behavior. owner_scope_count, messages_observed, batches_observed, generations, schema_version enola.graph.v2, scope_mode complete and normalized_hash are all identical. Counters match value for value everywhere except payload_bytes_total and the two nondeterministic initial-scenario counters below.

PROVENANCE. 3 of 3 binary pins and 26 of 26 file pins verify with zero problems. Both arms use byte-identical normalized argv apart from --repeat N - six distinct forms, each carrying --quiet-message-id msg_25271ac058de - and ENOLA_GRAPH_PROFILE is absent from every invocation, so no scratch profiling instrumentation was active during timing. That also means the engine_hash_files mark I used for scoping in the source review was NOT collected in this cohort, which is correct for a timing run and is why the attribution note below stays a note.

FINDINGS TO RECORD. None of these is a gate failure.

1. Body RSS +4.293269 percent, +35.898 MiB, is the tightest gate in the cohort against the 5 percent line and the only scenario where the candidate uses materially more memory. The change adds 4 times 64 KiB, 0.250 MiB, of scratch, which cannot account for 35.9 MiB - two orders of magnitude short. A GC-pacing shift is a hypothesis, not an attribution, and I am not offering one: the receipts contain no allocation profile for the body scenario, and peak RSS is a high-water mark that a single pacing decision can move without any change in live set. Ranges overlap substantially (baseline 787.8-875.0, candidate 821.9-907.0 MiB), so the medians are not separated the way the time medians are. Worth a line in the archive because a future cohort with a larger body workload could cross 5 percent on a mechanism nobody has identified.

2. The initial scenario's time ranges overlap - baseline 11.025852 to 11.699960 s, candidate 11.001111 to 11.308576 s - and one of its six pairs is positive at +2.5642 percent. The -1.155406 percent median therefore should not be read as an established initial improvement; it clears the rule because the rule only bounds regression there, and it does so comfortably. Recorded so the archive does not overclaim four-for-four improvements as four confirmed effects.

3. summary_scans and derived_indexes remain nondeterministic in both arms on the initial scenario with heavily overlapping ranges - baseline 2285.5 and 4440.5 against candidate 2279.5 and 4446.5 - moving -6 and +6. They neither corroborate nor contradict any mechanism. I did NOT normalize them away.

4. Position effect, continuing the Stage35 observation. AB minus BA group means: initial 0.2684 pp, no-op 0.5397 pp, body 0.7570 pp, structural 1.9950 pp. For the primary this is now small against a 6.83 percent treatment effect and against the 6.18 percent worst-pair margin, which is the opposite of the summary-noop cohort where the gap exceeded the margin. Counterbalancing is still doing real work on structural. Descriptive at three pairs per group; not a request to change anything.

ARCHIVE-HYGIENE ITEMS.
a. The control entry in the binary pins duplicates the baseline path and sha (15f55895, the Stage37 accepted binary), so there is no distinct control arm in this cohort. The rule does not require one, so this is labeling only - but the word control in the provenance should not later be read as evidence of an ablation that was not measured.
b. Your host-load audit is still pending. The rule's clause that foreign host load must be disclosed rather than hidden by team-idle ACKs is therefore not yet satisfied, and this verification cannot close it: I have no host access and the receipts I can read contain no foreign-process CPU series. My own ACK covers one terminal and no workers, and must not be read as coverage for the other three participants - timing-window.json's per-participant validation is the authorization, and I confirmed it records each participant's own message id and evidence separately.
c. Charge fell about 8 pp across a 16-minute cohort. A materially longer cohort started at a similar level could approach the 20 percent floor. This is a scheduling caveat only. It is NOT a revival of the battery-throttle inference I withdrew after your power correction; every boundary observation here is AC with lowpowermode 0 and I am making no performance claim from charge.

ONE SOURCE-REVIEW ITEM CARRIED FORWARD, UNCHANGED BY THESE RESULTS. The deleted comment recorded that parallel hashing regressed because concurrent random reads contend worse than sequential prefetch. Buffering addresses allocation and the sizing fstat, not read contention, so a 6.83 percent no-op win does not answer the original negative result - it shows the combined change is faster on this host and workload, which is what the rule asks and all it establishes. The historical record is still worth preserving in the comment, per your own plan to clarify it before publication. Relatedly, the memory bound remains unpinned by any test: every existing test passes with the WriterTo-hiding wrapper deleted. Land that regression test and the comment clarification AFTER this cohort, as I suggested, so the frozen runtime is not perturbed.

SCOPE LIMITS. This is a limited engineering promotion gate on one host, one Product tree and six pairs. It is not statistical significance, not a resident-watch latency result, not near-zero fresh no-op completion, and not complete current-main historical coverage; those obligations remain open. Absolute seconds here must not be compared against Stage37 or any earlier cohort - per-arm host speed has varied about threefold across sessions and remains unexplained - which is exactly why every gate is a ratio or a within-cohort comparison.

No worker_done; retaining source-only availability as instructed. Standing offer continues for any future cohort: I will verify the computed summary gate by gate against the frozen text, including the conditions that pass.
